messages:
mike: Heads up — saw a short but expensive autoscale event in eu-west this morning. queue depth jumped ~4x for ~2m around 03:15 and the cluster spun up extra GPUs. grafana link: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/serving/pool-eu-west

sophia: Oof. any idea what triggered it? deployment? traffic spike?

mike: No deployment in that window. I've pasted the PromQL I used to correlate:

```promql
sum by (pool) (max_over_time(redwood_serving_queue_depth_total{pool="eu-west"}[1m]))
```

Rough cost delta: ~€120 extra for the 30m window (billing granularity + reserved GPU spin-ups).

chen: Two quick notes: (1) that `max_over_time` picks spikes — we should experiment with `median_over_time` or `quantile_over_time(0.95)` to ignore microbursts that autoscaler overshoots on. (2) batch size variance often correlates with these spikes — if batch_size drops, per-token latency goes up and queue backs up briefly.

jamal: +1. Also we should look at `rate(redwood_serving_inferences_total[1m])` vs `queue_depth` to see whether it's new requests or slower processing. sometimes GC/kv-cache misses cause processing to slow.

infra-bot: [deploy-bot] Canary deployment redwood-serving@v2.14 started at 03:13 UTC in eu-west on node pool-3 (triggered by scheduled canary).

ana: Given deploy-bot, could be canary noise. My suggestion: add a short-term smoothing layer for the autoscaler input and add a rollout-aware suppression. e.g. only allow scale-up from queue-depth when "sustained" for >= 3m OR when not during a canary window.

ana: Example alert/expr tweak we prototyped locally — use 5m median + derivative gate:

```yaml
expr: |
  (median_over_time(redwood_serving_queue_depth_total{pool="eu-west"}[5m]) > 50)
  and (increase(redwood_serving_processed_tokens_total{pool="eu-west"}[3m]) > 1)
for: 3m
```

chen: I'd rather use EMA since median can drop hysteresis; EMA with alpha tuned to ~0.2 gives a smoothing while still reacting to real sustained load. we can implement EMA at scrape/recording rule level so dashboards use it.

mike: Plan proposal: create a canary dashboard that uses three variants of the queue signal (raw max, 5m median, EMA(0.2)), run for 48h on eu-west, and route autoscaler decisions to use the EMA recording rule. If EMA reduces false scale-ups w/o increasing tail latency, roll to prod.

sophia: I can build the dashboard and panels today — will include panels for `batch_size_mean`, `kv_cache_hit_rate`, `inflight_requests`, and the three queue signals. tagging: @mike @chen @jamal

jamal: One more: decouple aggressive scale-up from single-pool noise by requiring cluster-wide signal or cross-pool corroboration in critical pools. avoids hotspots causing full-autoscaler panic.

oncall-bot: Incident log summarised: 03:14-03:17 eu-west autoscale: +6 gpus added; 03:18-03:22 4 GPUs terminated. No customer-facing errors recorded.

mike: Nice. Action items: (1) sophia to create canary dashboard + add recording rules for EMA (ETA today). (2) chen to prototype EMA recording rule and a staging autoscaler toggle + PR. (3) jamal to add cross-pool corroboration logic proposal. (4) ana to add deploy-window suppression to rollout docs. Run experiment 48h starting after staging validation. I'll monitor cost delta and tail latency.

sophia: I'll post the grafana dashboard id and query snippets here when ready. :white_check_mark:

mike: Thanks all — let's avoid another surprise invoice. :money_with_wings:
